## Highlights

### totebag is now pure Rust, RAR included

RAR extraction now uses [`rars`](https://crates.io/crates/rars), a pure Rust RAR implementation, instead of the C UnRAR library (#95). RAR archives (RAR 1.3 through RAR 7) can now be listed and extracted by every build, with no extra Cargo feature and no C toolchain. Together with the zstd change below, `totebag` no longer needs to compile or bundle any C library. Entry names that would escape the destination directory (`..`, absolute paths, drive prefixes) are rejected, and Windows-style `\` separators in older archives are handled.

`totebag` can now also **create** RAR archives: `totebag -o out.rar <files>` writes RAR5 (the format WinRAR 5 and later read). `--level` maps onto RAR's compression methods:

| `--level` | RAR |
|---|---|
| 0 | store (no compression) |
| 1-9 | RAR's 1-5 (fastest to best); the default 5 gives RAR's own default, 3 |

Unix permissions and modification times are recorded, and empty directories are kept.

### `.tar.zst`: compression levels work again, in pure Rust

`.tar.zst` archives are now compressed with [`structured-zstd`](https://crates.io/crates/structured-zstd), a pure Rust zstd implementation that supports every zstd level. `--level` now affects `.tar.zst` output again (#96):

| `--level` | zstd |
|---|---|
| 0 | stored (no compression) |
| 1-9 | zstd levels 3-22, mapped linearly (the default 5 is level 13) |

In v0.9.0, the default pure Rust backend (`ruzstd`) only implemented zstd's fastest level, so `--level` 1-9 all produced the same output, and the released binaries were affected too. This release fixes that without bringing back a C dependency. Extraction also uses `structured-zstd`. Archives written by `zstd(1)` extract as before, and archives written by totebag pass `zstd -t`.

## Breaking changes

- **The `zstd-native` feature has been removed** from both `totebag` and `totebag-cli` (#96). It switched to the C zstd library, which is no longer needed. Remove `--features zstd-native` from your build commands (and `"zstd-native"` from the `features` of your `Cargo.toml` dependency), or Cargo will report an unknown feature.
- **The `rar` feature has been removed** from both `totebag` and `totebag-cli` (#95). RAR extraction is always available now, so drop `--features rar` (or `"rar"` from `features`) in the same way.
- **`Error::FeatureDisabled` has been removed** from the library's `Error` enum (#95). It was only returned for RAR when the `rar` feature was off. Code that matches on it must drop that arm.

## Bug fixes

- tar: entries whose path is longer than 100 bytes (stored with GNU long names / PAX) were listed and extracted under a name truncated to 100 bytes. Extraction then failed or wrote the file to the wrong path. Both listing and extraction now read the full name.
- Non-UTF-8 paths no longer cause a panic when an error message is displayed or when the format is detected from the file extension (#98, #102, thanks @nightcityblade).
- Shell completion generation no longer panics on a destination without a parent directory (#99, #101, thanks @nightcityblade).
- `totebag --help` no longer shows `[default: 5]` twice for `--level` (#97, #100, thanks @Jah-yee).

## Dependencies

- `kpea` (cpio) 0.2.5 → 0.4.0 (#87, #104).
- `ruzstd`, the optional `zstd` (C), and `tempfile` were removed; `structured-zstd` 0.0.59 was added (#96).
- `unrar` (C UnRAR) was replaced by `rars` 0.10 (#95). Every dependency is now pure Rust.

## Internal

- `Error::error_or` is now implemented in terms of `Error::error_or_else` (#104).

## CI

- The cross-compile action no longer takes a `features` input; release binaries are built with the default features, which now include RAR (#95).
- The release-published notification now fires; the release is published with the GitHub App token instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN` (#94).
